summary.text: Jerry Carl is a Mobile-born entrepreneur who served on the Mobile County Commission and represented Alabama's 1st Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2021 to 2025. He lost the 2024 Republican primary to fellow incumbent Barry Moore and won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary for the open seat. According to his campaign website, he is running as an ally of President Trump on immigration, gun rights and fiscal restraint.

paragraphs.text: Carl was born in Mobile, Alabama, and, according to his campaign website, started his first company at age 25. He has since started more than ten companies, ranging from real estate to healthcare, timber and the manufacture of church furniture.
His campaign website says he and his wife, Tina, have been married 44 years and have three children, and that he describes himself as an avid hunter.

According to his campaign website, Carl ran for the Mobile County Commission out of frustration with the direction of Mobile's local government; Ballotpedia lists his service on the commission as beginning in 2012. His campaign says he has eight years of local government experience and four at the federal level.

In 2020 he won the Republican runoff for Alabama's open 1st District seat over Bill Hightower, 52.3% to 47.7%, and then the general election over Democrat James Averhart with 64.4% of the vote. He was re-elected in 2022 with 83.6% against Libertarian Alexander Remrey.
In the House he served on the Armed Services and Natural Resources committees in the 117th Congress and on Appropriations and Natural Resources in the 118th.
After a court-approved congressional map moved Rep. Barry Moore into the 1st District, Carl and Moore met in a March 5, 2024 Republican primary, which Moore won 51.7% to 48.3%.
Carl returned in 2026 and won the August 11 Republican primary for the open seat with 74.6% of the vote, ahead of Austin Sidwell, John Mills and Lucas Burger.
